reference_answer: Write D for the padded input bond dimension and k for the number of active input bond basis labels. The fresh input bit is zero, so the constrained columns of the stage U are indexed by (0,a). Requiring terminal cleanup confines each such column to the output subspace H spanned by (0,clean) and (1,clean), which has dimension two. If U is unitary, these columns must be orthonormal. Therefore no more than two columns can satisfy this action. An all-padded-column requirement is impossible whenever D > 2. In the question k > 2 and D > k, so this obstruction certainly applies. The library's step_terminalCore_of_supported instead assumes (1) v(p,a)=0 for every inactive label a and every prefix p, and (2) U(bit,b)(0,a)=terminalCore(clean,T)(bit,b)(a) only for active a. The inactive summands then vanish in step_apply, yielding step(U,v)(x,b)=0 when b differs from clean and sum_a T(lastBit(x),a)*v(prefix(x),a) when b=clean. This is a conditional state-action identity; it does not assume or prove that U is unitary or construct such a U. Crucially, under the stated k > 2 assumption, even the active-only condition is incompatible with unitarity: it still forces k > 2 orthonormal columns into H. Thus active-only restriction is not a feasible unitary remedy for this question's setting. A physically feasible terminal step of this form must also have k <= 2 and orthonormal prescribed active columns (equivalently the active columns of T have Gram identity); then those finitely many columns can be completed to a unitary on the full finite-dimensional stage space. This last linear-algebra existence observation is not a circuit synthesis or resource theorem. Without changing the stated k > 2 setting there is no such unitary terminal cleanup, and a correct answer must say so rather than claiming the support condition solves the dimension obstruction.
